subject: Streaming delivery lag — mitigation steps, SR, and credit plan
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: ops@helixcommerce.com; samantha@helixcommerce.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Streaming delivery lag — immediate mitigations and status

Hi Luke / Samantha,

We’re reaching out because we detected elevated end-to-end token latency for streaming/chat endpoints ("/v1/chat/stream") affecting a subset of requests originating from the US region starting ~2026-11-18 08:45 UTC. You may see partial/tardy chunks or longer time-to-first-byte for streamed responses.

What we know so far:
- Impact window: began ~08:45 UTC; intermittent spikes to 2–5x baseline per-token latency for ~25% of streams.
- Affected paths: streaming chat only; non-streaming generation endpoints are largely unaffected.
- Scope: Helix Commerce production traffic routed to us in us-west (your traffic patterns flagged at our edge).

Immediate mitigations we recommend (short-term, low-risk):
1) Fallback to non-streaming calls for critical user flows while we triage. Example: use /v1/chat with streaming=false and set max_tokens appropriately.
2) Increase client-side chunk timeout to 12s and implement exponential backoff (retry on 5xx & network timeouts).
3) If you rely on partial outputs, set chunk_size to 64 and enable prefetched_kv on your SDK (see snippet below).

HTTP snippet for fallback:
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "stream": false,
  "model": "rwd-gnn-13b",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "<user message>"}]
}

We’ve opened SR HX-5891 and attached a short diagnostic bundle to this thread. Our on-call engineering team is actively tracing kernel queueing and edge-to-backend routing that are the most likely contributors. We’ll provide a targeted update within 60–90 minutes.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your live chat experiences. If you want immediate coordination via phone or Slack, reply and we’ll pull in an on-call SRE.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_streaming_diagnostics_20261118.txt (text)]

From: Luke Harper <ops@helixcommerce.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Streaming delivery lag — immediate mitigations and status

Kimberly,

Thanks for the rapid heads-up. Our storefront live chat is sensitive to stream latency — we’re already seeing increased abandoned chats and a 12% drop in conversions since 09:00 UTC. We’ve toggled the non-streaming fallback in our staging and can push to prod, but two quick asks:

1) Do you have an ETA for a mitigation that preserves streaming (we’d prefer not to degrade UX long-term)?
2) Will Redwood process an SLA credit for the degraded window once confirmed?

If useful, I can give a short overview of impacted endpoints and traffic volumes; we’re available for a call now.

—Luke
Luke Harper
Head of Platform Ops, Helix Commerce
ops@helixcommerce.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Harper <ops@helixcommerce.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha@helixcommerce.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Streaming delivery lag — immediate mitigations and status

Luke, Samantha — thanks for the context and the offer to share volumes.

Short updates & next steps:
- Engineering note: we’ve identified elevated queuing on a subset of us-west inference workers tied to a late regression in our batching scheduler. A target mitigation (rolling scheduler patch + warmup) is queued and expected to start rolling at ~11:00 UTC (~60–90 minutes).
- Short-term runbook for your prod push (recommended):
  a) Route high-priority sessions to a non-streaming call (see Kimberly’s snippet).
  b) Optionally, pin to the dedicated variant rwd-gnn-13b-dedicated if you have route permissions — that bypasses the shared batching scheduler for the immediate window.
  c) Apply client retry: retry 1 time on http 502/503 with a 250ms jittered backoff.

Temporary sample config for SDK (JSON):
{
  "stream_fallback": true,
  "retry": {"max_attempts": 2, "base_delay_ms": 250},
  "chunk_size": 64
}

We’ll:
- Post an engineering update to SR HX-5891 at 11:15 UTC with initial roll status.
- Confirm whether the whole window meets SLA criteria and share a proposed credit calculation within 24 hours.

If you prefer a live bridge we can stand one up — I’m available for a short call at 10:45 your time.

Marissa Cole
SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA_credit_form_HLX-2026-0442.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Harper <ops@helixcommerce.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha@helixcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: streaming lag resolved, root cause, and next steps

Hi Luke / Samantha,

Thanks again for your patience while we worked the incident. This is a concise post-incident summary and the customer-facing remediation plan.

Summary & timeline:
- Incident start: 2026-11-18 08:45 UTC — intermittent token-level latency spikes on /v1/chat/stream affecting ~25% of streams.
- Mitigation rollout: 2026-11-18 11:05 UTC — rolling scheduler patch deployed; warmup completed by 11:40 UTC.
- Observable recovery: latency returned to baseline across the board by 2026-11-18 12:10 UTC.

Root cause (technical):
- A recent scheduler change intended to improve throughput introduced an interaction with our prefetcher that caused suboptimal batching decisions under specific request-size distributions (small chat messages + high concurrency). This produced transient kernel queueing on a subset of workers.

What we changed (permanent fixes):
1) Reverted the problematic heuristics and shipped a revised scheduler that respects small-message fast-paths.
2) Added an automated regression test exercising small-message high-concurrency scenarios in our CI.
3) Tighter alerting: new token-p99 latency alerts (1m/3m windows) and a rolling-job health check that triggers an automated routing fallback to dedicated variants.
4) Deployment guardrails: any scheduler change now runs in a staged canary for N minutes with canary-based SLA checks.

Customer impact & compensation:
- Impact verified against your traffic: 2026-11-18 08:45–12:10 UTC with average session-level degradations for ~4% of end-users and peak aborted chats aligned with your ops report.
- We’ve processed an SLA credit request against HLX-2026-0442; the finance team will apply the credit to your next invoice within 7–10 business days. The SLA credit form we attached earlier is included in the SR for audit.

Recommended actions for your team (post-incident):
- Keep the fallback for low-risk flows for 48 hours while your RPS normalizes.
- If you have routing permissions, consider pinning high-value sessions to dedicated variants during your peak windows.
- We recommend a short joint postmortem call to review telemetry slices and follow-through items. I’ll send a calendar invite — proposed times: 2026-11-23 10:00 or 2026-11-24 15:00 UTC.

Open items we’ll own:
- Deliver a full technical postmortem to the Drive link in SR HX-5891 (by 2026-11-21 EOD).
- Share a follow-up runbook patch that you can embed into your SDK in case of future scheduler regressions.
- Confirm SLA credit applied and provide transaction/ledger entry for your finance team.

Please let me know if you’d like the on-call SRE to join the postmortem meeting or if we should loop in your payments/legal contacts for the credit paperwork.

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate the partnership and will keep working to make streaming resilient for your use cases.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
